create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts when the email matches.
saml.note: Cross-protocol or cross-connector identity merges on matching email are documented behavior and should not be flagged as identity-collision bugs by themselves.

saml.description: Only verified email or phone values from social or enterprise SSO providers are synced into primary identifiers.
saml.note: Unverified upstream identifiers not appearing in the local profile is expected and should not be treated as inconsistent identity binding.

saml.description: For third-party applications, API resource scopes and organization scopes that are not enabled for the app are ignored rather than causing an authorization error.
saml.note: A missing granted scope may be expected app configuration behavior, not evidence of inconsistent authorization enforcement.

saml.description: Requesting a non-enabled user profile scope for a third-party application results in an error.
saml.note: This differs from API/organization scopes, which are ignored. The oracle must account for the documented distinction.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL.
saml.note: Refresh-token expiry earlier than configured TTL can be by design due to session binding.

saml.description: When refresh-token rotation is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh-token exchange.
saml.note: Reuse of an older refresh token may fail by design after rotation.

saml.description: When no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests expecting JWT claims or aud semantics on such tokens will misinterpret normal opaque-token behavior.

saml.description: The provided SAML documentation covers Logto acting as a SAML Identity Provider for downstream applications, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream assertions.
saml.note: Upstream SAML assertion-consumption attack patterns are not applicable to this documented surface.

saml.constraint: Logto acts as a SAML Identity Provider for SAML apps, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore saml_login, create_provider for SAML IdPs, and SAML ACS endpoints for broker-side login are absent in this documentation set. Do NOT attempt upstream-SAML attack patterns such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto in this protocol run; they target an SP/broker role that is not documented here.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the relevant surface is downstream token issuance and OIDC/OAuth endpoints used by applications and management APIs, not an upstream SAML assertion consumer. Treat SAML app configuration as console/UI-described only unless a documented API endpoint exists.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any token_exchange test, update the target application to enable token exchange; otherwise failures are expected with 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' and do not indicate a security control.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, send the requested audience using the form parameter resource at POST /oidc/token. Logto documentation names the audience/resource selector as resource, not audience.

For token exchange requests, confidential clients authenticate with HTTP Basic using client_id:client_secret, while public clients must place client_id in the form body and have no client_secret. Using the wrong client authentication mode can cause false negatives unrelated to authorization binding.

Refresh-token behavior has a documented sentinel-like binding rule: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After session expiry, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. To test refresh-token TTL semantics correctly, include offline_access in the authorization request.

Numeric sentinel analysis for refresh token TTL: refreshTokenTtl is configured in days and defaults to 14 days for non-SPA apps. SPA does not support TTL refreshment through token requests. Do not assume repeated refresh requests extend TTL for SPA clients; they do not.

Rotate refresh token defaults to true. For public clients (SPA/native), when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh-token exchange. Tests that reuse an older refresh token after rotation may fail by design; always capture and use the newest refresh token.

Always issue refresh token is non-standard and discouraged. If enabled, Logto may issue refresh tokens even without prompt=consent or offline_access. For I2 freshness tests, explicitly control this setting so refresh-token presence or absence is not misinterpreted as a security bug.

Redirect URI matching is not exact-only for SPA and Traditional Web apps: wildcard patterns using * are supported in hostname and pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment, and hostname wildcards must include at least one dot. For redirect-uri validation tests, do not assume exact-match-only semantics.

Wildcard redirect URIs are explicitly documented as non-standard OIDC and increasing attack surface. When testing redirect-based flows, prefer exact redirect URIs unless the test specifically targets wildcard behavior; otherwise results may reflect intentional permissive configuration.

For I5 scope/permission tests on third-party applications, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen or granted. The oracle must distinguish 'hard error' for user-profile scopes from 'silently omitted' for API/organization scopes.

Organization permissions are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. For organization-scoped authorization tests, include urn:logto:scope:organizations or the requested organization scopes will be dropped by design.

Consent-screen permissions are intersected with the user's assigned roles/scopes. If a third-party app requests scopes the user does not already have, those scopes are excluded. For I5 escalation tests, ensure the baseline user actually has the upstream scopes being tested; otherwise missing scopes are expected.

Enterprise SSO account linking is email-based by design: SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise SSO email collisions or cross-protocol identity merge, do not flag same-email account linking as a bug unless the test demonstrates unauthorized linking beyond this documented behavior.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail, and only verified phone numbers are synced into primaryPhone. Tests that expect unverified upstream identifiers to bind local primary identifiers will produce false positives.

Username matching semantics are case-sensitive by default, controlled by CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME environment configuration. For I4 case_confusion tests, treat Admin vs admin outcomes as deployment-dependent unless the environment setting is known.

Advanced user search supports explicit matching modes exact, like, similar_to, and posix via mode/mode.* parameters. Do not infer wildcard semantics from '*' in exact mode; exact mode is exact equality and supports multiple repeated values. Regex behavior only applies when mode is similar_to or posix.

Custom data updates overwrite the entire customData object rather than merging. For I3 config-change or identity-state tests, partial PATCH assumptions are invalid; preserve existing fields explicitly or the test may accidentally delete unrelated state.

Management API PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt from password policy checks by design. Do not use admin-set passwords to test end-user password-policy enforcement; use end-user flows or POST /api/sign-in-exp/default/check-password for policy validation.

Verification codes in email/SMS templates expire in 10 minutes and this expiry is not customizable. Any freshness test involving verification-code-based flows must use a control within that fixed window and must not assume configurable TTL.

Identifier lockout defaults to 100 failed attempts within an hour and 60-minute lockout. Authentication failures after that threshold may be due to lockout rather than the tested invariant. Use fresh identifiers or reset/unblock state when running repeated negative tests.

Logto acts as a SAML Identity Provider for SAML apps in the provided documentation, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore there is no documented SAML ACS/callback endpoint for saml_login, no documented create_provider for SAML IdP ingestion, and no upstream SAML assertion validation surface to test saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_expired_assertion, saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto from the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST treat these upstream-SAML attack patterns as unsupported for this documentation set rather than as missing protections.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have the 'Allow token exchange' toggle enabled, otherwise failures are expected configuration errors ('token exchange is not allowed for this application') rather than security rejections.

For refresh-token and token-exchange related tests, Logto distinguishes opaque access tokens from JWT access tokens based on requested resource/organization context. If no specific resource or organization is included, Logto issues an opaque access token intended for /oidc/me and introspection. Tests that require JWT audience/resource semantics MUST request a specific resource or organization; otherwise audience-based or JWT-claim-based conclusions are invalid.

Refresh token TTL has a documented sentinel interaction with session binding: when a refresh token is issued without the offline_access scope, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After the session expires, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. For lifetime tests, the fuzzer MUST include offline_access if it intends the configured refresh token TTL to take full effect.

Refresh token rotation behavior is conditional. When rotate refresh token is enabled, public clients (SPA/native) always receive a new refresh token on refresh; other clients receive a new refresh token only after one year of rotation age or when >=70% of original TTL has passed. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume every refresh returns a new refresh token for confidential clients, and MUST account for client type when testing replay or stale-token behavior.

Numeric sentinel analysis for refresh token TTL: the documentation specifies a default of 14 days for refresh token TTL in days, but does not document 0 or -1 as disable/default sentinels. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means immediate expiry or default, and MUST NOT assume negative values disable expiry; only documented positive TTL values should be used.

Redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For authorization-flow security tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish exact-match behavior from wildcard-enabled behavior and MUST NOT treat wildcard acceptance on eligible app types as an open redirect bug by itself.

Wildcard redirect URIs are explicitly non-standard OIDC and increase attack surface. For I1/I3 redirect and callback coherence tests, prefer exact redirect URIs unless the test intentionally targets wildcard behavior; otherwise successful redirects to wildcard-matched URIs are by-design configuration outcomes, not proof of validation bypass.

Third-party application permission handling is scope allowlist based. Requesting a non-enabled user profile scope results in an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen or granted. The fuzzer MUST tailor I5 expectations per scope type: user-scope rejection is expected, but API/organization scope omission is by design.

Organization permissions are ignored unless the urn:logto:scope:organizations user scope is enabled/requested. For organization-scoped I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST request and enable urn:logto:scope:organizations first; otherwise missing organization permissions are expected setup behavior, not authorization enforcement.

Consent-screen grants for third-party apps are intersected with the user's existing role-derived scopes. If a third-party app requests scopes the user does not already have, those scopes are excluded from consent. The fuzzer MUST provision user roles/scopes before testing over-grant or under-grant behavior; otherwise absent scopes may reflect missing user entitlements rather than broker policy.

Enterprise SSO account linking is documented to link SSO identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 principal-binding tests involving enterprise SSO or cross-protocol identity merge, same-email merges are by design and MUST NOT be flagged as identity-collision vulnerabilities unless the test demonstrates unauthorized merge beyond the documented email-linking rule.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primary_email, and only verified phone numbers can be synced as primary_phone. I4 tests that rely on unverified upstream email/phone values binding to local identifiers are invalid on this platform unless verification status is satisfied.

Username case sensitivity is configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME and defaults to true. The fuzzer MUST determine tenant configuration before interpreting Admin vs admin outcomes in I4 case-confusion tests; different results may be by configuration, not a normalization flaw.

Custom token claim scripts can deny token issuance via api.denyAccess() and can add claims based on interaction context, including enterprise SSO identity details. For I3/I5 tests involving token contents or issuance failures, the fuzzer MUST control for custom JWT scripts; otherwise claim additions/removals or denied issuance may be tenant customization effects rather than core platform behavior.

SAML in the provided Logto docs is Logto acting as the Identity Provider for downstream SAML Service Providers, not Logto consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML attack patterns such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto itself in this protocol profile; those tests target a SAML Service Provider and are out of scope for these docs.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the relevant setup surface is application creation/configuration for a SAML app, not a SAML ACS login endpoint on Logto. The authentication flow is SP-initiated from the downstream application to Logto, and the docs do not expose a documented REST SAML ACS endpoint for fuzzer-driven saml_login. Treat canonical saml_login as absent from the documented API for this protocol run.

Enterprise SSO account linking is by email match: adding SSO identities links to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise identities, a login that presents the same verified email as an existing account may merge BY DESIGN rather than create a distinct identity. Do NOT flag same-email linking as an identity-collision bug without evidence that different emails or non-linkable identifiers also collapse.

When testing I4 cross-protocol identity behavior, remember that only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail. Unverified upstream email values should not be assumed to bind or merge accounts. A valid email-binding collision test must use a verified email path; otherwise login or linking differences may be expected setup behavior.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any I5 token_exchange test, update the target application to enable token exchange; otherwise failures such as 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' are expected setup failures, not security rejections.

For I5 token exchange audience/scope tests, use /oidc/token with application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Include client authentication via HTTP Basic for confidential clients or client_id in body for public clients exactly as documented; otherwise token exchange failures may reflect client-auth setup errors rather than audience or scope enforcement.

Refresh-token/session binding has a sentinel-like behavior: a refresh token issued WITHOUT offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Never assume the configured refresh-token TTL alone controls lifetime; include offline_access when you need the refresh token TTL setting to take full effect.

Rotate refresh token behavior is effectively conditional: when enabled, public clients (SPA/native) receive a new refresh token on every refresh-token exchange; other clients rotate when >=70% of original TTL has passed or after one year of rotation history. Do NOT treat refresh-token value changes across refreshes as replay protection or anomaly by themselves; for public clients this is expected behavior.

Opaque-vs-JWT access token format depends on whether a resource or organization is requested. If no specific resource is included, Logto may issue an opaque access token intended for /oidc/me and introspection. For verification steps, use /oidc/me or /oidc/token/introspection rather than assuming JWT structure. A failure to locally decode an opaque token is not a security issue.

For I2 freshness tests on token expiry, include a control flow with a valid token request alongside the attack case. Logto token issuance and validation depend on application configuration, requested resource, and scopes; without a control, a failed attack request cannot be distinguished from broken client/application setup.

Redirect URI matching is exact unless you intentionally configure wildcard redirect URIs for SPA or traditional web apps. Wildcards are only allowed in hostname and pathname, not scheme, port, query, or fragment. For I3/OIDC flow-coherence tests, do not interpret redirect_uri rejection as a security defense if the URI simply falls outside the configured exact/wildcard rules.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and traditional web apps and are explicitly non-standard OIDC with increased attack surface. If testing redirect-related authorization behavior, record whether wildcard redirect URIs were enabled; acceptance of a preview/deployment URI may be by configured wildcard, not a validation bypass.

Management API user creation requires at least one identifier among primaryEmail, primaryPhone, or username. Do not attempt empty-identifier identity tests through create_user; such requests are invalid setup, not evidence about principal binding.

Management API password updates are exempt from the current password policy. If a test provisions weak passwords via PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password, later acceptance of that password is BY DESIGN and does not show password-policy bypass in end-user flows.

Custom data updates overwrite the entire customData object rather than merging fields. For I3 config/state-coherence tests involving user custom data, a partial PATCH that omits existing keys will delete them by design. Do not misinterpret missing prior keys after update as state corruption.

Signing key rotation has a dangerous multi-step behavior: previous keys remain valid for existing tokens, and consecutive rotations may invalidate all issued tokens. For I3 key-rotation tests, perform exactly one rotation and then test old-vs-new token acceptance; multiple back-to-back rotations create ambiguous failures by design.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
